lab_title: Structural Anatomy of the Heart and Blood Flow Pathway
top_level_objectives: Identify the four heart chambers, four valves, and major vessels entering and leaving the heart.
Trace the complete path of blood through pulmonary and systemic circulation.
Explain how valve placement and action prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle.
Compare right and left ventricular wall thickness and relate structure to pumping workload.

scenes.brief_purpose: Establish anatomical orientation and introduce the heart as a dual pump connected to major vessels.
key_visuals: Life-size 3D heart model in anatomical position
Anterior/posterior orientation cues
Color coding for deoxygenated and oxygenated blood
Visible aorta, venae cavae, pulmonary trunk/arteries, and pulmonary veins
student_actions: Rotate around the heart model and identify anterior, posterior, superior, and inferior directions.
Tap highlighted major vessels to preview their names and whether they carry blood to or from the heart.

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students identify the four chambers and distinguish right versus left heart anatomy.
key_visuals: Cutaway heart revealing right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle
Labels appearing one chamber at a time
Septum separating right and left sides
Blue right-side chambers and red left-side chambers
student_actions: Select each chamber when prompted by name.
Compare atria and ventricles by location, size, and role in receiving or pumping blood.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the four valves and connect their positions to prevention of backflow.
key_visuals: Close-up cutaway of tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, and aortic valves
Animated valve leaflets opening and closing
Arrows showing permitted flow direction
Backflow attempt blocked by closing valve animation
student_actions: Tap each valve to hear/see its name, location, and flow direction.
Predict whether a valve should be open or closed during filling versus pumping phases.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the right-heart pathway from systemic venous return to pulmonary circulation.
key_visuals: Blue animated blood particles entering through superior and inferior vena cava
Pathway through right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, and pulmonary arteries
Lung silhouettes connected to pulmonary arteries
Stepwise glowing pathway segments
student_actions: Guide or sequence the blue blood-flow path by selecting structures in order.
Correctly place labels for the venae cavae, right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, and pulmonary arteries.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the left-heart pathway from pulmonary venous return to systemic circulation.
key_visuals: Red animated blood particles returning from lung silhouettes through pulmonary veins
Pathway through left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and aorta
Systemic body outline receiving blood from the aorta
Color transition at lungs from blue to red
student_actions: Build the oxygenated pathway by tapping structures in correct order.
Explain why pulmonary veins are shown carrying oxygenated blood despite being veins.

scenes.scene_name: 6. Ventricular Wall Thickness and Pumping Load
scenes.brief_purpose: Relate myocardial structure to function by comparing right and left ventricular walls.
key_visuals: Transverse section through both ventricles
Measurement markers showing thinner right ventricular wall and thicker left ventricular myocardium
Pulmonary loop shown as short, low-resistance route
Systemic loop shown as longer, higher-resistance route
student_actions: Measure or compare the relative thickness of the two ventricular walls.
Match each ventricle to the circulation it pumps into and justify the difference in muscle thickness.

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate chamber, valve, vessel, and flow knowledge in one complete sequence.
key_visuals: Full cutaway heart with all structures initially unlabeled
Blue and red flow arrows through the complete circuit
Checkpoint markers at chambers, valves, and vessels
Optional beat-cycle animation showing valves opening and closing
student_actions: Arrange the complete blood-flow sequence from vena cava to aorta.
Identify all four chambers, four valves, and major vessels in a timed or self-paced review.
Respond to short prompts about valve function and right-versus-left ventricular workload.
